collectionMethod: Read-only fetch of the three public Synthetic pages. Plan cards and the default Standard token table were read from rendered HTML, including line-through marks. billingMeter.headline: One subscription for every model. Credits regenerate over the week and apply at discounted model rates.
billingMeter.quotaShape: One weekly credit pool shared across models. The Tokens/mo column is an estimated monthly token count per model if that model is used under the stated mix. Rows are alternatives, not a sum.
billingMeter.debitVersusList: Usage-based requests pay the usage-based price. A subscription debits the weekly rate limit at the subscription discounted rate. The API $/mo column is the page's estimated monthly value at the usage-based price, not the discounted debit.
billingMeter.overage: All three public plans say "Allows extra usage at API pricing".
billingMeter.noFiveHourOrMonthlyLimitSentence: Synthetic only uses weekly limits. Unlike other services, there aren't additional five-hour or monthly limits.

weeklyRegeneration.visibleSentence: Every 202 minutes (about 3.4 hours), you get back 2% of your total weekly credit limit. That means it takes one week to fully regenerate from zero.
weeklyRegeneration.roundingFlag: The visible copy says 202 minutes. The rate-limits payload says 201.6 minutes. 50 ticks of 201.6 minutes is 10,080 minutes, which is 7 days. 50 ticks of the rounded 202 minutes is 10,100 minutes. This file keeps both numbers and does not convert either into a monthly token quota.

fastMode.quote: Turn on fast mode and your requests run up to 2× faster. While it's on, each request uses 2× as much of your rate limit.

infiniteMode.quote: Built for background agents: infinite mode requests never count against your rate limit, in exchange for running much slower. (Currently DeepSeek V4.1 Flash only.)
infiniteMode.notAnUnlimitedAllowance: The pricing table still publishes a finite Tokens/mo and API $/mo for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on Big (8,108,108,108 tokens, API $754). Infinite mode is a slower path that does not debit the rate limit for that limited model. It is not an unlimited adopted value.

upToMonthlyUsagePayload.saleNote: The pricing payload sale field was undefined, so no active promotional price was served. A Kimi K3 first-month sale string exists in the client bundle and did not render.
upToMonthlyUsagePayload.visibilityCaveat: These ceiling strings are in the server payload. The captured static HTML of /pricing does not contain a visible sentence "up to $90", "up to $300", or "up to $900", and the downloaded pricing client bundle does not reference the property name upToMonthlyUsageByPlan. The ceilings equal 10 times each catalog monthly price (including unpublished Bigger at $300 → "3000"). They are not the per-model API $/mo figures. Standard's highest published API $/mo in this capture is $251, which is below 300.
upToMonthlyUsagePayload.doNotTreatAsUniform10x: Usage-based price divided by the discounted rate is different for each model and for input, cached input, and output. Examples from the captured table: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is 10× / 10× / 4×; Kimi K3.1 Pro is 2× / 2× / about 1.43×; GLM-5.3 is 3.5× / about 3.71× / 2×; GLM-5.3 Flash is 1.5× / 2× / 2×.

weeklyVersusMonthlyFlag.sourceConventionKept: The public meter is a weekly pool. The table header the page actually publishes is Tokens/mo, with the tooltip "Estimated monthly tokens". Exact integers are stored in publishedTokens. The rendered Standard abbreviations are stored in standardTableDisplay. Go and Big were not the selected tab in the initial HTML; their integers come from the same payload.
weeklyVersusMonthlyFlag.bundleFormulaNotUsedAsAMonthlyQuota: The client catalog sets weeklyCreditQuotaCents to Math.round(700 * monthlyPrice / 30), which is 210, 700, 2100, and 7000 cents for Go, Standard, Big, and Bigger. This file records that formula and those cent values. It does not multiply them into a second monthly token number.
weeklyVersusMonthlyFlag.upstreamMismatch: A weekly regenerating pool and a Tokens/mo column do not tell this repo which month length to adopt. No weekly-to-monthly factor is chosen here.

consistencyCheck.result: For every captured model and every plan key, discounted blended value of the published token count equals the plan monthly price exactly ($9 / $30 / $90 / $300). Usage-based blended value floors to the published API $/mo integer.
